title: Generative interfaces
evidenceStatus: Three finished authored initial trees, three retained earlier attempts, one recorded state-preserving server revision, offline lifecycle probes, and four passing BYOK tests
summary: Jev genuinely composes and edits a tree from 10 to 12 prepared recipes, while code owns every component's content, binding and action. Offline probes show current-version selection resets draft data, a late settings result overwrites an apartments session, and shortlist only displays a success notice. The evidence mixes old catalogue rules and a separate layout-classification study, so it does not establish reliable multi-step interaction.
strengths: Real tree selection, placement and edit operations run through a catalog-constrained composer and fixed React registry.
Bound inputs and an inert preview support normal revisions; one recorded cloud edit removes a toggle while preserving an edited name.
The composer preserves user state without automatically including raw state in evaluator inputs.
Earlier incomplete attempts remain published, and the page acknowledges prepared content and local demonstration actions.
Four BYOK tests pass with 71 assertions covering credential and transport behavior.

findings.title: Version selection resets the current draft
findings.evidence: experience-prototypes/src/generated-ui.tsx:330 keys StateProvider by epoch with spec.state; :365 increments epoch on any version click. probes/ui.json supplies User-edited draft through the observer, reselects the current version, and sees key 1 become 2 with initial name Alex Morgan and no external store.
findings.impact: Layout history and replay can discard entered values, contradicting the central preserve-edits question even though the normal server revision path preserves state.
findings.fix: Keep canonical user data in a stable external store per session. Version structure separately, avoid remounting active versions, and make restoring historical data an explicit action.

findings.title: Unbound stream results overwrite another session and incomplete streams retain active labels
findings.evidence: src/generated-ui.tsx:392 changes domain without aborting live composition; :278 installs all snapshots. probes/ui.json starts settings, switches to apartments, then accepts the old settings tree as Live Jev composition. A stream ending after one step remains Jev is composing with no interruption notice.
findings.impact: The selected domain/version can disagree with the rendered tree, and visitors cannot reliably distinguish an incomplete attempt from active or successful generation.
findings.fix: Bind every request and replay to domain, base version and session revision; abort/invalidate on navigation. Require explicit terminal outcomes for finish, limit, unavailable, cancellation, errors and premature EOF, preserving partial work on an incomplete branch.

findings.title: Save and shortlist acknowledge success without stateful outcomes
findings.evidence: src/generated-ui.tsx:337 handlers only call setNotice. probes/ui.json announces Sunlit studio added to your shortlist without adding a collection. ui-catalog.ts:149 binds budget, but apartment records at :159 have no eligibility/filtering logic.
findings.impact: Successful rendering and status text do not establish that the generated interface helps complete an application task. Entered preferences have no downstream effect.
findings.fix: Add deterministic draft/saved preferences, stable selected IDs, validated save behavior and computed affordability/commute status. Let Jev select presentation and order while code owns data, calculations and effects. Score independently inspected action outcomes.

findings.title: Evidence mixes catalogue versions and a different classifier without a workflow scorer
findings.evidence: results/composed-ui.jsonl has 3 finished initial trees and 3 earlier attempts; settings/event lack catalogue versions and use column 2/3 times versus current maxUses=1 at ui-catalog.ts:132. record.ts:128 reuses finished rows without config hashes and :142 drops terminal decisions. main.tsx:658 loads old ui metadata while :672 loads composed-ui. Legacy ui has 20 planned, 12 complete, 12 matching layouts and 9 preserved labels; stored 0.60/0.45 rates conflate missing outcomes with quality.
findings.impact: Historical trees remain renderable but do not reproduce current candidate rules. Layout classification and one successful server edit cannot establish generated-action correctness or multi-step preservation. Synthetic final-tree replay is not an actual event/timing trace.
findings.fix: Use one manifest for current composition evidence; keep historical classifier metrics separately labelled. Hash candidate/catalog/composer/protocol identities, retain all terminal choices, attempts and costs, invalidate stale checkpoints, replay actual snapshots, and score independent multi-step workflow postconditions.

findings.title: The wrapper and composer disagree on the batch strategy name
findings.evidence: server/compose.ts:15 allows batched, while installed @json-render/core/dist/index.js:3724 allows batch. Actual offline wrapper probes reject batched with Unknown composition strategy and batch with Invalid composition request before any provider call.
findings.impact: The working sequential default remains usable, but batch creation and controlled latency/call-count comparisons are blocked.
findings.fix: Derive the request enum from the pinned composer type or translate it explicitly; add mocked tests for both supported strategies, edits and invalid inputs, and record evaluator calls separately from primitive choices.

simulation.title: An apartment decision desk
simulation.description: Compare six synthetic apartments, edit budget and commute, save preferences and maintain a shortlist, then revise section order and visibility while switching layout branches. Include a cancelled stream and an unsupported booking request to expose the capability boundary.
simulation.jevsRole: Select prepared presentation recipes, grouping and ordering using candidate descriptions plus explicitly approved derived context. It cannot invent records, perform application actions or change arbitrary bindings.
simulation.codeRole: Own canonical preferences and saved snapshots, apartment data, selected IDs, affordability/commute calculations, action validation, tree checks, branch/request identity, stream terminal states and independent outcome scoring.
acceptanceCriteria: All six rendered apartment records preserve supplied prices and commute facts.
Shortlist changes an inspectable set exactly once and removal reverses it.
Save produces a visible validated snapshot separate from draft preferences.
Inputs and selected IDs survive reorder, hide/show, layout history and replay; restoring old data is explicit.
Late responses cannot overwrite another domain or branch.
Cancellation and failure leave a usable prior layout and accurate terminal status.
Unsupported booking requests cannot produce a success notice.
Visitors can inspect tree changes, decisions, the baseline and independently measured outcomes separately.

evaluation.design: Author 30 development and 120 held-out workflows balanced across three domains and six task families. Each contains creation, three revisions and intervening user edits/actions. Freeze independent semantic postconditions, allowed tree alternatives, immutable data and action outcomes. Three candidate-order/paraphrase seeds give 360 workflows and 1,440 composition sessions per protocol. Compare sequential creation/edits with repaired batch creation/sequential edits: at current budgets the pair has 2,880 sessions and at most 46,800 logical evaluator requests before retries, 28,800 sequential plus 18,000 batch-create. Use 10,000 paired bootstrap resamples clustered by original workflow, preserving all seeds/revisions. Require zero data resets or stale writes in 1,000 offline sequences and held-out workflows, a 95% lower supported-workflow success bound of at least 90%, and zero observed false successes on unsupported tasks. Use exact rare-failure bounds: zero failures in 20 independent negative workflows has a one-sided 95% upper bound of 13.9%, insufficient for a below-2% claim, which needs at least 149 independent negative workflows with zero failures. Compare batch using a two-percentage-point correctness noninferiority margin and positive latency-reduction interval. Follow with native-control/keyboard/accessibility checks and a counterbalanced 12-person, eight-task usability study. No proposed model or participant run was performed during this audit.
baselines: Fixed complete form/comparison using identical supplied data.
Deterministic rule-based command parser over the same candidates.
Current sequential Jev composition versus batch creation with sequential edits.
Oracle operation planner to isolate renderer and state-management failures.
metrics: Semantic postcondition and complete-workflow pass rates, required-field recall, and irrelevant-control count.
Valid bindings, action outcomes, unsupported-request recognition and change scope outside the request.
Field/shortlist preservation, stale writes, replay correctness and explicit stream terminal outcomes.
Availability and limit stops separately from conditional semantic quality.
First usable preview and completed-workflow latency, evaluator calls, choice slots, attempts, cost and payload bytes.
Clustered paired 95% intervals by family, viewport interaction checks, automated accessibility findings and keyboard/focus review.
Participant completion time and final errors on counterbalanced tasks.

coverage.current: Three finished prepared initial trees, three retained prior attempts and one recorded server revision preserving a name/removing a toggle. Separate legacy classifier has 20 planned cases, 12 completed, 12 matching layouts and 9 preserved layout labels. No complete-workflow scorer exists.
coverage.full: Proposed held-out coverage is 120 workflows, three presentation seeds, creation plus three revisions, and two model protocols: 2,880 composition sessions with a current-budget upper bound of 46,800 logical evaluator requests before retries. No external split or official benchmark score is claimed.
coverage.feasibility: No large dataset or weights are required. Full coverage needs independently reviewed workflow labels, session/action repairs, versioned candidates, a checkpointed runner and a future provider budget. A ten-workflow preflight estimates actual volume but does not replace complete evaluation.

libraries.name: json-render controlled StateStore
libraries.use: Reuse createStateStore and StateProvider store to keep canonical session data stable while Jev changes tree structure; retain bounded candidate composition and existing catalog validation.

libraries.name: fast-check
libraries.use: Generate and shrink edit/compose/navigate/replay/cancel/action sequences under Bun against a small independent session model to expose data-loss and stale-response failures.

libraries.name: axe-core
libraries.use: Check rendered revisions for automated accessibility violations, paired with manual keyboard/focus and task-outcome checks. This evaluates code/rendered output rather than assigning accessibility authority to Jev.

nextSteps.action: Separate canonical data from layout versions; add domain/branch/request identity and explicit terminal stream outcomes.
Implement inspectable save/shortlist state and deterministic apartment eligibility calculations.
Correct current evidence wiring, configuration/checkpoint identity, terminal trace retention and historical classifier labels.
Fix batch strategy spelling and add mocked protocol coverage.
Build the independently labelled multi-step suite and run complete paired protocols after offline checks pass.
Build the apartment decision desk and reuse its session/version machinery in adaptive forms and structured-document editing.
